item.title: Beyond the Menu: Seabourn Is Making Destination-Inspired Dining Part of the Journey
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For luxury travelers, discovering a destination often begins at the table, and Seabourn is expanding that connection with the introduction of Earth & Ocean, a culinary philosophy that brings regional flavors, exceptional ingredients and food-focused exploration into the cruise experience. Building on the Earth & Ocean restaurant concept introduced in 2018, the philosophy will influence menus and programming across the fleet, pairing locally inspired dishes with carefully selected gourmet ingredients from around the world. In The Restaurant, a new Chef’s Market Finds approach will highlight regional ingredients and specialties reflecting each ship’s itinerary, from wild seafood in Alaska to fresh snapper in Australia and New Zealand. The program will also extend beyond onboard dining through chef-led experiences, local market visits, regional seafood celebrations, scenic cruising brunches and other culinary encounters designed to introduce guests to the food traditions and distinctive flavors of the destinations they visit.

The Curated Take

Food can offer one of the most immediate and memorable ways to understand a place. A regional ingredient, a traditional preparation or the influence of a particular coastline can reveal something about a destination that extends well beyond its landmarks. Seabourn’s Earth & Ocean philosophy recognizes that connection, making culinary discovery an integral part of the voyage rather than simply an onboard amenity. For travelers who value both exceptional dining and a deeper sense of place, the approach adds another dimension to luxury cruising, bringing the character of each destination to the table.

item.title: Discover Australia Through the Stories of Its First Peoples
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Australia’s most meaningful cultural journeys often begin with the people who know its landscapes best. The latest edition of Connect to Country, the digital publication from Discover Aboriginal Experiences, invites travelers to explore the country through the knowledge, traditions and perspectives of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander guides. Issue 12 journeys from the ancient rock art landscapes and rainforests of the Worimi people to sunrise experiences at Uluru, a Djiringanj ceremony on Yuin Country in New South Wales, and an early morning cruise through Kakadu’s Yellow Water Billabong. Other stories explore the enduring relationship between coastal communities and oysters, the history of the pearl trade on Western Australia’s Dampier Peninsula, and the ways Traditional Custodians have sustained their cultures through generations of change. The edition also connects luxury travelers with First Nations-led experiences paired with stays from Luxury Lodges of Australia, demonstrating how cultural understanding can become an essential part of a sophisticated Australian travel experience.

The Curated Take

Cultural travel becomes richer when the experience moves beyond observing a place to understanding the people, histories and traditions that have shaped it. First Nations-led tourism offers an opportunity to encounter Australia through perspectives that cannot be found in a conventional destination guide, from ancient knowledge of the natural environment to stories carried through dance, food, language and ceremony. For luxury travelers, these experiences bring depth and context to journeys through Australia’s extraordinary landscapes, while placing the voices of Traditional Custodians at the center of the story.

item.title: Where Christmas Grandeur Meets the Warmth of the Blue Ridge Mountains
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The Blue Ridge Mountains provide a memorable setting for a holiday escape, and Asheville, North Carolina, is welcoming the 2026 festive season with a mix of grand traditions, mountain-town celebrations, culinary experiences and creative discoveries. The season’s signature attractions include the 131st Christmas at Biltmore, with its illuminated estate and candlelit evenings, Winter Lights at the North Carolina Arboretum, and the National Gingerbread House Competition at Omni Grove Park Inn. Beyond the familiar celebrations, visitors can discover a more contemporary side of the holidays through Warren Haynes’s Christmas Jam, local artisan markets, hands-on glassblowing and jewelry-making workshops, and seasonal dining across the city. Families can enjoy performances of The Nutcracker and Frozen, while couples and wellness-minded travelers can retreat to mountain-view saunas, historic hotel fireplaces and festive rooftop lounges. With celebrations extending into January, Asheville also makes an appealing destination for a post-Christmas getaway, combining the warmth of Appalachian holiday traditions with the region’s distinctive arts, food and hospitality.

The Curated Take

The most memorable holiday destinations offer more than a calendar of seasonal events. They create an atmosphere that invites travelers to slow down, reconnect and discover something unexpected. Asheville brings together the nostalgia of a grand estate dressed for Christmas, the creative energy of an independent arts community and the natural beauty of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Its appeal lies in that balance: a destination where a festive getaway can be as lively or restorative as the traveler chooses, with enough variety to make a multigenerational holiday feel personal rather than prescribed.

item.title: Costa Rica’s Casa Chameleon Is Bringing Boutique Hotel Service to Private Oceanview Villas
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For travelers who want the freedom of a private residence without giving up the attentive service of a luxury hotel, Casa Chameleon at Las Catalinas is introducing a new way to experience Costa Rica’s Pacific coast. Beginning January 2027, four exclusive five-bedroom branded residences will join the property’s offering, perched along a scenic ridgeline above the car-free coastal town of Las Catalinas in Guanacaste. Each villa accommodates up to 10 guests and features a private oceanview plunge pool, rooftop garden, multiple terraces and expansive indoor-outdoor living spaces. Managed by the team behind the Relais & Châteaux member and Two Michelin Key boutique hotel, the residences offer dedicated concierge service, access to the hotel’s dining experiences and assistance arranging private chefs, in-residence spa treatments and personalized activities. Guests can also enjoy the surrounding destination, from protected tropical forest and coastal trails to the Pacific’s sheltered bays, wellness offerings and the walkable town itself.

The Curated Take

The appeal of a private villa is often the freedom to gather, settle into a destination and create a rhythm of one’s own. Casa Chameleon adds another layer by bringing the service culture and hospitality of an established luxury hotel into a residential setting. With just four residences, the experience is particularly suited to multigenerational families, milestone celebrations and groups of friends who value both shared spaces and personal privacy. Las Catalinas also offers a distinctive setting, where a car-free coastal town, protected natural surroundings and access to outdoor experiences create a sense of place beyond the villa itself.

item.title: Forget Just Food and Drinks: This Maldives Resort Is Making All-Inclusive About the Experience
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Holiday Inn Resort Kandooma Maldives, an all-inclusive island escape is expanding well beyond meals and beverages to encompass the experiences that make a Maldives holiday memorable. The 146-villa resort has introduced an experience-led offering that brings together ocean adventures, diving, traditional fishing, wellness, and island dining. Qualifying stays include a sunset cruise, daily group reef snorkeling, sunrise line fishing, and one scuba dive per day for certified divers, along with a choice of massage at Kandooma Spa by COMO Shambhala. With 28 dive sites accessible from its PADI 5-Star Dive Centre, including the renowned Kandooma Thila, the resort offers opportunities to explore the marine life of the South Malé Atoll. Guests can also enjoy dining across multiple island venues, from casual poolside meals to beachside dining and a 24-hour café, alongside a changing program of activities for adults and children. The approach reflects a broader idea of all-inclusive travel: making it easier for guests to discover more of the destination without having to plan every experience separately.

The Curated Take

The Maldives is often associated with private villas and pristine beaches, but the most memorable island stays offer reasons to venture beyond the shoreline. Kandooma’s expanded all-inclusive concept puts the surrounding ocean and local traditions at the center of the experience, with sunrise fishing, reef exploration, and diving woven into the rhythm of a stay. The inclusion of wellness and family activities adds another dimension, making the resort an appealing option for travelers who want both relaxation and a sense of discovery. It is an approach that makes the destination itself part of the holiday, rather than simply the backdrop.

item.title: Beyond the Private Island: South Africa’s New Vision of the Luxury Wellness Safari
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Just two and a half hours from Cape Town, a different kind of South African safari experience is taking shape at Kuganha, an ultra-luxury retreat set across 10,000 hectares of rewilded land in the Cape Tankwa Karoo. Opened in March 2026 following a three-year redevelopment, the property combines private Big Five safari experiences with an unusually comprehensive approach to wellness. Its 10 Private Restoration Suites, each spanning 320 square meters, feature dedicated in-suite spa facilities, including a sauna, steam and salt therapy, cold plunge, flotation experience, outdoor pool and private relaxation spaces. A full-time wellness therapist, private safari ranger, personalized dining and dedicated concierge service further distinguish the experience. Beyond its intimate scale, Kuganha’s story is rooted in nearly three decades of conservation and habitat restoration, offering guests an opportunity to encounter South Africa’s wildlife within a landscape shaped by ecological renewal.

The Curated Take

The next evolution of luxury safari travel may be less about how far a guest can escape and more about the quality of the experience once they arrive. Kuganha brings together two forms of restoration: the ecological renewal of the land and the personal renewal made possible by time, privacy and thoughtful wellness. Its combination of private safari, expansive tented suites and individual spa facilities creates an alternative to the conventional lodge experience, while its conservation history gives the setting a deeper sense of purpose. For travelers pairing Cape Town with a South African safari, Kuganha offers a compelling reason to venture beyond the familiar routes.

item.title: A Once-in-a-Decade Journey: Experience Germany’s Oberammergau Passion Play in 2030
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Every ten years, the Bavarian village of Oberammergau becomes the setting for one of Europe’s most extraordinary cultural traditions. First performed in 1633, the Oberammergau Passion Play brings the story of Christ’s final days to life through a production featuring local residents, preserving a community tradition that has continued for nearly four centuries. For its 2030 performance season, custom tour operator Audley Travel has created a bespoke itinerary that places the experience within a wider journey through Germany and Austria. The 10-day route pairs the celebrated production with Munich’s complex history, the Alpine landscapes surrounding Innsbruck, the lakes and villages of Austria, and Salzburg, the birthplace of Mozart. With stays in Oberammergau or nearby Bavarian villages, the journey offers an opportunity to experience the Passion Play alongside the region’s cultural heritage and mountain scenery.

The Curated Take

Some journeys are defined by where they go; others by the rare experiences that give them meaning. Oberammergau’s Passion Play belongs to the latter. Its once-in-a-decade staging offers travelers an opportunity to witness a living tradition shaped by generations of local participation, while the surrounding Bavarian and Austrian landscapes provide a rich cultural counterpoint. For travelers drawn to heritage, history, and meaningful European experiences, 2030 presents an especially compelling reason to explore this corner of the Alps.

item.title: This Mexican Wine Country Escape Is Bringing New Recognition to Valle de Guadalupe
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Thirteen years after its founding, El Cielo Valle de Guadalupe continues to shape the growing appeal of Mexican wine tourism, offering travelers an immersive introduction to the vineyards, cuisine, and hospitality of Baja California. Conceived as a boutique hotel surrounded by vineyards, the destination has evolved into an integrated winery and resort where guests can explore the winemaking process through vineyard tours, cellar visits, and guided tastings. Its villa-style accommodations are set among gardens, lakes, and mountain scenery, while restaurants such as Latitud 32 and Polaris bring regional ingredients and culinary traditions to the table. The anniversary comes during a notable year for the property: El Cielo Resort received One MICHELIN Key in 2026, and the integrated winery, vineyards, and resort earned B Corp Certification for its approach to business, community, and environmental responsibility. Together, these milestones add to Valle de Guadalupe’s growing reputation as a destination for travelers seeking a more distinctive experience of Mexico, shaped by wine, food, landscape, and local culture.

The Curated Take

Valle de Guadalupe offers a different perspective on luxury travel in Mexico, one that moves beyond the familiar coastal resort experience and into the country’s evolving culinary and wine culture. El Cielo brings together the pleasures of a vineyard stay with opportunities to understand the people, traditions, and production behind Mexican wines. Its latest recognitions are noteworthy, but the destination’s deeper appeal lies in the way it connects hospitality to the character of the region. For travelers interested in food and wine journeys with a strong sense of place, Baja California deserves a place on the itinerary.

item.title: What Happens When You Mix Japanese Onsen Culture with Nordic Design?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Copenhagen is about to welcome a distinctive new waterfront destination as KAI, a Japanese-inspired water culture house designed by Kengo Kuma & Associates, prepares to open on December 5, 2026. Located on Paper Island in the Danish capital’s inner harbor, the striking new attraction brings together ten pools, saunas, steam bathing, cultural spaces, and year-round outdoor swimming. Its standout feature is a heated onsen overlooking the harbor, offering a Japanese approach to bathing against the backdrop of Copenhagen’s evolving waterfront. The architecture is equally distinctive, with five brick towers constructed from 300,000 handmade bricks rising above a light-filled glass structure. Inside, visitors will find everything from family-friendly pools and fitness facilities to warm-water therapy and cold plunges, while an outdoor pool nestled between the towers invites bathing beneath the open sky. Additional harbor swimming areas and a timber waterfront deck are expected to follow in early 2027, further connecting the development to the city’s public spaces and maritime heritage.

The Curated Take

Copenhagen has long understood how to make its waterfront part of everyday city life, and KAI adds an intriguing new dimension to that relationship. Rather than treating wellness as something reserved for a resort, the project brings bathing, architecture, and cultural gathering into the heart of the city. Its combination of Japanese onsen inspiration and Danish design creates a distinctive experience for visitors, while its public character reflects Copenhagen’s broader commitment to accessible urban spaces. For travelers planning a winter city break, KAI offers another reason to linger in the Danish capital beyond its celebrated restaurants, museums, and design scene.

item.title: This Australian Luxury Travel Collection Is Opening New Doors to the Country’s Most Extraordinary Landscapes in 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From the Great Barrier Reef and Tasmania’s Freycinet Peninsula to Western Australia’s Ningaloo Coast and the remote East Kimberley, a series of major investments is reshaping the future of luxury wilderness travel across Australia. Members of Luxury Lodges of Australia are preparing a new chapter of openings, refurbishments, private accommodations, and small-ship expeditions throughout 2027. Orpheus Island Lodge has already reopened following an extensive refurbishment, while Saffire Freycinet will introduce Saffire Jewel, an expansive private villa designed for families and small groups, in December 2026. Further ahead, Sal Salis Ningaloo Reef is scheduled to reopen in March 2027 with refreshed eco-luxury wilderness tents and guest spaces, followed by the May reopening of Bullo River Station after a major redevelopment of its remote outback homestead. May also marks the 40th anniversary of True North Adventure Cruises, which will introduce new expeditions exploring Western Australia’s Rowley Shoals and the Great Barrier Reef. Together, these developments offer fresh reasons to plan a luxury Australia itinerary built around extraordinary landscapes, private guiding, marine encounters, and access to places far beyond the usual travel routes.

The Curated Take

Australia’s most compelling luxury experiences often begin where conventional travel becomes more difficult. What distinguishes this collection is not simply the standard of its accommodations, but the access each property provides to a particular landscape, community, or ecosystem. From the marine wilderness of Ningaloo and the Great Barrier Reef to Tasmania’s dramatic coastline and the vast cattle country of the Kimberley, these investments reinforce the appeal of journeys shaped by place rather than a checklist of destinations. For travelers considering Australia in 2027, the developments also create an opportunity to combine several distinct lodge experiences into one richly varied journey.
